messages:
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout rlv3 v3.2.0 -> eu-west-1 (10% traffic) at 2115556667 :rocket:

ryan (support): seeing a pile of 429s from three enterprise customers — creating tickets, forwarding logs. sample: `429 /v1/generate customer_id=acct_42 token=abc...`

sarah (oncall): paging oncall + sla. i'm looking at the alerts, spike started ~2115556700. tagging @matt and @jess.

matt (eng): thanks — last deploy introduced a change to exemption list parsing for token headers (migrated to a CSV blob). possible mismatch between header names we expect and what the code reads.

jess (sre): confirmed: alert rate graph: 429 rate x10 for canary hosts vs baseline. here's a quick query: `count(status=429) by host where deploy=v3.2.0` -> host-canary-3 is hot.

ryan (support): customers reporting timeouts then 429s. one customer says: "we're getting quota errors even for internal service-to-service calls". high priority ticket escalated.

matt (eng): digging into the new parser — seems when exemptions CSV includes CRLF lines we drop the first header token, so `authorization` ended up parsed as `\rauthorization` and never matched. that explains missing exemptions for s2s tokens. 

sarah (oncall): can we flip the feature flag that gates the CSV parser? need immediate mitigation.

matt (eng): yes. patch: flip `rlv3:exemptions_parser_enabled` -> false. curl to flip: 
```
curl -X POST https://config-api.internal/flags/rlv3/exemptions_parser_enabled -d '{"value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```
I'll run now.

matt (eng): flipped flag at 2115556802 :white_check_mark:

jess (sre): traffic to canary dropping 429s but still some elevated errors. looks like some requests were already routed to the new path and hit token accounting mismatch. running backfill rules.

matt (eng): additional mitigation: adding a temporary whitelist rule for affected customer IDs in redis rate-limit-exemptions: `SADD rl:exemptions:acct 42 77 108` — applied at 2115556838.

eva (infra): routing note: I’ve rebalanced upstream routing so 100% of traffic for those enterprise accounts goes to stable cluster (rlv2) while we verify. running a partial rollback of canary hosts as well.

deploy-bot: initiating canary rollback of host-canary-3 -> draining at 2115556860 :arrows_counterclockwise:

incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2115556667 — rate-limit regressions during rlv3 canary. paging oncall.

oliver (product): drafting customer comms: short note saying we mitigated, apologize for interruption, and will provide root cause and ETA for full fix.

jess (sre): quick log snippet for context:
```
[2115556721] host-canary-3 GET /v1/generate 429 token=\"\rauthorization:Bearer abc\" customer=acct_42 rt=12ms
[2115556723] host-canary-3 PUT /v1/usage 200 user=svc-int
```
Shows the CR prefix.

sarah (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall matt for postmortem/cleanup. I'm going offline after followup with customers.

matt (eng): confirming next steps: 1) revert CSV parser change with proper CRLF handling in source; 2) add unit test for headers with CRLF; 3) schedule full rollback verification and canary retest behind toggled flag; 4) postmortem in #postmortems with timeline; 5) customer notif + credit as needed.

jess (sre): current status: traffic normalized for affected customers, remaining alerts are informational. closing pager for now but keeping watch for 2h.

ryan (support): customers notified with interim message; they want ETA for permanent fix. I'll coordinate.

matt (eng): pushing hotfix branch `fix/exemptions-crlf` -> will roll to canary after tests and enable flag when ready.

oliver (product): noted potential product impact: internal service-to-service calls and dedicated tenant quotas. will include in comms.

sarah (oncall): thanks all — filing incident ticket with timeline and assigning to @matt and @jess for full RCA. closing thread for active mitigation. :lock:
